# Debug handle checks


The originals, and a BlitzLLVM program compiled without `-d`, carry on when a command is given the handle of something that was never made, was freed already or is 0 (the result of a load that failed): most commands do nothing or give 0, and some stop the program. A bug like that usually shows far from where it was made. A debug build (`blitzcc -d`) stops at the command that got the handle, with the line of the command and a message like

```
Runtime Error: TextureWidth: the texture 3 does not exist (never made or already freed).
Runtime Error: PlaySound: the sound is 0, which is no sound (was it made, or did it fail to load?).
```

What a debug build checks, on top of what every build already refuses (banks, files and streams, brushes, entities, surfaces, fonts, gadgets, timers, samplers and images that do not exist stop the program everywhere):

| Handle | Commands | Release build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Texture | `FreeTexture` of a freed texture or 0, `TextureWidth`, `TextureHeight`, `EntityTexture` and `BrushTexture` with a texture that does not exist | ignored, 0 and ignored |
| Image | `FreeImage` of an image that is freed already or 0 | ignored |
| Sound | every sound command with the 0 of a sound that failed to load | ignored |
| Channel | every channel command with a channel that was never given out | ignored |
| Movie | every movie command with the 0 of a movie that failed to open or a movie that was closed | ignored, 0 |

The 0 that a failed load gives counts as a handle that does not exist, so `FreeTexture`, `FreeImage`, `FreeSound`, `CloseMovie`, `FreeFont`, `FreeTimer`, `FreeGadget` and `FreeTreeViewNode` of 0 stop a debug build as well (freeing, closing and deleting must be given something that exists); `FreeEntity`, `FreeBrush`, `FreeBank`, `CloseFile`, `Delete` and the like already stop every build. What stays legal: `EntityTexture` and `BrushTexture` with the texture 0 (which takes the texture off), and a channel that is over, as channels end by themselves. `Object.Type(handle)` gives `Null` for a handle that names no object in every build, as the language says.

A debug build also ignores [AsyncLoading](AsyncLoading), [AsyncSaving](AsyncSaving) and the environment variables `BLITZLLVM_ASYNC_LOAD` and `BLITZLLVM_ASYNC_SAVE`. A file that can not be loaded or decoded then stops the program at the command that loaded it, and a save that fails tells so in the result of the command that asked for it. The commands themselves keep working: [TextureReady](TextureReady), [ImageReady](ImageReady) and [EntityReady](EntityReady) always give 1, and [SavesPending](SavesPending) always gives 0.
